analysis: Every one of the 236 non-associative products has a witness (G*H)*K not isomorphic to G*(H*K) with factors of at most 3 vertices (product orders 2: 144 codes, 4: 84, 8: 8), and every one of the 224 non-commutative products a witness G*H not isomorphic to H*G; all 460 witnesses are certified by edge count or degree sequence. Associativity and commutativity up to isomorphism are therefore no weaker than the strict notions (bold H-C14-1 survives).
assumptions: witness search over the 7 graphs with 1-3 vertices (all triples / pairs, ordered by total order), escalating to graphs with <= 4 vertices if needed
isomorphism decided exactly (invariants, then networkx VF2)
falsification: A non-strict code without any witness (then it would be associative/commutative only up to isomorphism, refuting H-C14-1, and would be examined by hand).

hypothesis: H-C14-1 (bold): no - for local products, associativity and commutativity up to isomorphism are equivalent to their strict versions; for every one of the 236 non-associative (224 non-commutative) products a witness exists among graphs with at most 3 vertices.
methodology: For each non-strict code, search the smallest triple (G,H,K) with (G*H)*K not isomorphic to G*(H*K), and the smallest pair with G*H not isomorphic to H*G.
question: Can a local product satisfy (G*H)*K = G*(H*K) (or G*H = H*G) up to isomorphism for all graphs although the canonical map is not an isomorphism?
